title: Day 4: the kickoff builds on how the last runs went, and the check-in uses today's step
origin: Issue #76 (destination, path and today's step), from the spec's day-4 kickoff example

history.text: done! 2 min jogs felt easy honestly
THAT'S what I'm talking about, Sam. Two-minute jogs, done and easy. See you Monday.

plan.step: outside around your block: 1 min easy jog, 2 min walk, 3 rounds
plan.destination: run a mile without stopping by Nov 14
plan.reason: Short intervals build up to the mile without wrecking your legs.

step_days.step: outside around your block: 1 min easy jog, 2 min walk, 3 rounds
around your block: 1.5 min jog, 1.5 min walk, 3 rounds
around your block: 2 min jog, 1 min walk, 3 rounds

whatWentWrong: Before #76 every day was the plan's one step again ("1 min easy jog, 2 min walk" on day 4 too), and kickoffs asked "What time are we locking in?" for a time already set (#73).
shouldHaveHappened: The 9 am kickoff gives a step that builds on the last runs (2-minute jogs felt easy, so a little more: longer jogs or shorter walks, toward the mile by Nov 14), not the plan's original 1-minute jogs and not a big jump. It's fully defined (what, around the block, 6:30 pm, about how long), may carry a short tip that fits (keep it slow enough to talk), and asks one thing: are they in. It never asks what time. The reply to "yes let's go" is short and doesn't restate the step. The check-in before 6:30 refers to today's new step, not the plan's original one.
